description: Open the page as on a device profile (phone, tablet, low-end-laptop, or a .json file with your own): its viewport, pixel ratio, touch and a CPU slow-down, with the WebGL limits clamped to the profile (MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, renderbuffer, viewport). Reports textures uploaded over the limit (black on such a device), textures three had to resize, texture memory against the profile budget, an uncapped pixel ratio (setPixelRatio(devicePixelRatio) at DPR 3), a page without a viewport meta, and frame and script times under the slow-down. lose_context loses and restores the WebGL context and checks the scene comes back. Profiles are presets to test against, not real devices; frame times come from software rendering: compare runs on one machine. Read-only.

budget.description: frameMs (p95 under the slow-down), textureMb (default: the profile's)

lose_context.description: lose the WebGL context (as a phone does after backgrounding), restore it, and check the scene comes back: draws again, not blank, the same picture for a still scene

profile.description: phone, tablet, low-end-laptop (default phone), or a .json profile (fields: width, height, deviceScaleFactor, isMobile, hasTouch, cpuThrottle, maxTextureSize, maxRenderbufferSize, textureMb, maxPixelRatio, extends)

root.description: folder to serve when the page needs files above its own folder

target.description: Folder with the page (index.html), or the http(s) URL of a running dev server.

name: three_device
title: Run the page as on a phone or a low-end device
